_comment: English bodies for smolagents (framework). Mechanism per C0-1..6. Official English quotes kept verbatim. layer_position/providers not rendered — not included.

axes.model_access:
**The official self-description is model-agnostic: "supports any LLM"** (README, verbatim).

The implementation is several Model classes, each covering one end:

- On the HF side, `InferenceClientModel` goes through the Hub's Inference Providers. Officially named:
  Cerebras, Cohere, Fal, Fireworks, HF-Inference, Hyperbolic, Nebius,
  Novita, Replicate, SambaNova, Together

- The rest go through `LiteLLMModel` (officially "100+ different models"), `OpenAIModel` (OpenAI and compatible endpoints,
  examples given for Together / OpenRouter), `AzureOpenAIModel`, `AmazonBedrockModel`

- On the local side: `TransformersModel`, `MLXModel`, `Ollama`

**Switching providers = swap one Model class.** A `provider=` parameter also works. The code structure stays the same.

**Unknown: after switching providers, the reliability alignment of tool calling / structured output is not stated by the official docs.**
(guided_tour and the models reference page checked.)
axes.runtime:
**A pure Python library. You run the agent loop yourself in a local process. No hosted execution service officially.**

The official positioning, verbatim (README):

**Official wording**: "run powerful agents in a few lines of code"

Install `pip install smolagents` (Python ≥3.10).
It ships two CLIs: `smolagent` (general multi-step CodeAgent, with an interactive wizard) and `webagent` (a helium-based web-browsing agent).

Hierarchical multi-agent systems are expressed with `managed_agents=` for delegation.

The whole agent can also be shared to HF Hub as a Gradio Space via `agent.push_to_hub()`
(README, verbatim: "share your agent to the Hub, as a Space repository").

But that is only a **share / load form** — **not a vendor-hosted resident runtime** — the process stays in your hands.
axes.local_files:
**The framework itself presets no file-system tools.**

The official default toolbox (`smolagents[toolkit]`) has only three items: DuckDuckGo/WebSearch,
a Python code interpreter, Whisper transcription — **no dedicated file read/write tool**.

CodeAgent reads and writes files through **the Python code it generates itself** (e.g. `open()`) or custom tools you provide.

So **the file boundary comes from the execution environment, not the framework**. Locally it is constrained by
`LocalPythonExecutor`'s import allowlist. In a remote sandbox it is confined to the sandbox container. The two sandbox modes are on the secure_code_execution page.

**Unknown: the default file-access scope allowed for CodeAgent is not stated by the official docs.**
(secure_code_execution and guided_tour pages checked; no file-permission section.)
axes.background:
**Self-hosted = stop the process and it's gone; no hosted background option.**

All run modes in the README are local code calls. The forms are Python API / CLI / sandbox. There is no cloud-resident or scheduled-execution form.

**The only official mechanism related to "long tasks / checkpoints" is single-step execution.** `agent.step(memory_step)` advances one step at a time.
Memory lives in-process at `agent.memory`. The use case on the tutorials/memory page is exactly:

**Official wording**: "tool calls that take days"

**Unknown: the official docs provide no built-in way to persist this memory and restore it in a new process** (tutorials/memory and
guided_tour pages checked).

So resuming after interruption means serializing steps yourself.
axes.tools:
**The tool surface is wide, and MCP is first-class access.** The README self-describes as "Tool-agnostic", with four tool sources:

- ① Custom tools — the `@tool` decorator or subclassing `Tool`
- ② **MCP** — `ToolCollection.from_mcp(...)` reads any MCP server (install `smolagents[mcp]`)
- ③ LangChain tools — `Tool.from_langchain`
- ④ **HF Hub Spaces as tools** — `Tool.from_space`

The default toolbox (`smolagents[toolkit]`) = DuckDuckGo/WebSearch, Python code interpreter, Whisper transcription.

Multi-agent systems use `managed_agents=` to treat sub-agents as callable units.
There are also `final_answer_checks` for custom termination validation.
axes.context:
**Context = the step history (AgentMemory); no cross-session persistence.**

The official tutorials/memory page says the
agent "has a memory of past steps".

Step types: `TaskStep` / `ActionStep` / `PlanningStep` / `FinalAnswerStep`.

Three official manipulation options:

- `agent.replay()` to replay
- read/write `agent.memory.steps` directly (the example even moves steps between two agents)
- `step_callbacks` (official example: delete old screenshots to save tokens)

There is also `planning_interval=N` to insert a planning step every N steps.

**The official docs position this axis as "inspect / rewrite memory", not compression.**

**Unknown: deep context management like spilling large tool outputs to disk is not stated by the official docs.**
(tutorials/memory and guided_tour pages checked.)
axes.permissions:
**The official docs are very blunt about execution safety. The default `LocalPythonExecutor` is not a secure sandbox.**

README, verbatim:

"The built-in `LocalPythonExecutor` is **not** a security sandbox. It applies some restrictions but can be bypassed and must not be used as a security boundary."

What the local interpreter provides:

- step-by-step AST execution
- **imports denied by default** (open an allowlist with `additional_authorized_imports`)
- **submodules denied by default** (`numpy.*` to allow all subpackages)
- loop iteration caps
- undefined operations error out

**For real isolation you must use a remote sandbox**: `executor_type="blaxel" / "e2b" / "modal" / "docker"`.

The official docs distinguish two modes: sandbox only the code snippets; or put the whole agent in the sandbox (the latter required for multi-agent).

There is also a Human-in-the-Loop example (examples/plan_customization), but **it is not a built-in approval mechanism**.

**Unknown: network access control is not stated by the official docs.**
axes.fit:
**Fits these four scenarios.**

- You buy into code-as-action (officially "30% fewer steps" than JSON tool calling) and are willing to sandbox LLM-generated code
- You want model-agnostic access including local models (transformers / Ollama / mlx-lm)
- You want a thin, hackable library; Python stack
- You want the MCP / LangChain / Hub Space tool ecosystem

**Does not fit these three scenarios.**

- You need a vendor-hosted resident background or checkpoint resume (pure library; memory is not persisted)
- You want neither arbitrary-code-execution risk nor a remote sandbox
- You want batteries-included preset file system / memory / sub-agent orchestration

sections.与 OpenAI Agents SDK 的分野：动作怎么表示:
Both belong to the "primitives" tier, but the carrier of actions differs:

| Dimension | **smolagents** | **OpenAI Agents SDK** |
|---|---|---|
| Action carrier | **Python code snippets** (CodeAgent) or JSON (ToolCallingAgent) | function calls (function tools / handoffs) |
| Official efficiency claim | "uses **30% fewer steps**" (citing arXiv 2402.01030) | no comparable quantification given |
| Execution risk | LLM code must run in a **sandbox** | tool calls, not arbitrary code |
| Switching providers | swap the Model class | swap the `model` string / adapter |

**In one line**: want "actions as code" and can sandbox the code → smolagents. Want tool calls +
built-in guardrails/human-in-the-loop → OpenAI Agents SDK.
sections.CodeAgent vs ToolCallingAgent（官方对比）:
The official guided_tour explains the two clearly:

| | **CodeAgent** (default) | **ToolCallingAgent** |
|---|---|---|
| Action format | Python code snippets | structured JSON |
| Strengths | high expressiveness, composable/loops/transforms, emergent reasoning | reliable, validated arguments, maps well to external APIs |
| Weaknesses | syntax/exception handling needed, needs a secure execution environment | lower expressiveness, actions must be predefined, no code synthesis |
| Fits | problem-solvers needing reasoning / chaining / dynamic composition | atomic tools, scheduler / controller style tasks |
sections.沙箱：安全边界官方说得很清楚:
The README states the default interpreter's positioning directly:

> The built-in `LocalPythonExecutor` is **not a security sandbox**. It applies some restrictions
> but can be bypassed and must not be used as a security boundary.

What the local interpreter provides:

- step-by-step AST execution
- imports denied by default (`additional_authorized_imports` allowlist)
- submodules denied by default (`numpy.*` to allow all subpackages)
- loop iteration caps
- undefined operations error out

For real isolation the official docs give two sandbox classes:

- **hosted cloud sandboxes**: Blaxel, E2B, Modal (`pip install 'smolagents[blaxel|e2b|modal]'`)
- **self-hosted containers**: Docker (`executor_type="docker"`)

**Keep the two modes apart**: sending only code snippets into the sandbox (simple, but unavailable for multi-agent);
or moving the whole agent (model and tools included) into the sandbox (stronger isolation, but you pass credentials and set it up manually).
sections.与 HF Hub 的关系：分享，不是托管:
In the README, agents and tools are both Hub objects:

- `agent.push_to_hub("user/agent")` publishes the agent as a **Gradio Space**
- `agent.from_hub(...)` loads community agents; same for tools

Multi-agent systems use `managed_agents=` (plus the official `ManagedAgent` wrapper class) for hierarchical delegation.

> ⚠ **This is not "vendor-hosted execution"**: a Space is a share/load form; the agent loop still runs on your side,
> and there is no "keeps running after shutdown" semantics. Don't mistake it for a hosting service when selecting.

All eight axes of this entry have conclusions. But items remain that **the official docs genuinely don't state**,

related: **The pair most worth contrasting**: both "primitives" tier; the divide is action representation (code-as-action vs function calls). One has built-in guardrails/HITL; the other requires you to bring your own sandbox.
Another coding base from a model vendor; but that one wraps an existing CLI, while smolagents is a library where you write the loop yourself.

The opposite contrast: CrewAI is an orchestration layer with the Crew/Flow dual abstraction; smolagents is thinner — just an agent library + `managed_agents` delegation, no state-machine orchestration.
